criteria.note: warp_llm_runner.py exists at plugin/templates/scripts/runners/llm/. It reads a JSON journey (prompt_id, cases of id/input/graders/fake, optional budgets, baseline), drives each case through a provider callable defaulting to fake_provider (which returns the case's canned output/cost/latency), grades, aggregates pass_rate/total_cost/total_seconds, checks budgets and regressions. I drove it over both shipped fixtures: pass.journey.json exited 0, fail.journey.json exited 1 naming the regressed case. fake_provider verified to echo per-case blocks (ALPHA vs BETA distinct), so grading is real and an adopting repo can pass its own provider=.

I confirmed each grader kind fails loud and names case+grader: contains ('output does not contain'), not_contains ('unexpectedly contains'), equals ('expected X, got Y'), regex ('did not match output'), and an unknown kind ('unknown grader type'). Each also passes when satisfied (grading not always-fail). A case with no graders key AND a case with explicit graders:[] both fail loud ('a case that asserts nothing is not proof', exit 1). Cost-over-budget, latency-over-budget, and pass-rate-below-min each fail with the measured value named (0.0300 exceeds 0.02; 2.5000 exceeds 1.0; pass rate 0.500 is below 1.0).

Regression detected only when prompt_id differs from baseline.prompt_id. With prompt v3 vs baseline v1, a baseline-passed case that now fails is reported 'regression: case refund passed under prompt v1 but fails under prompt v3' and the run exits 1 even though the greeting case passed. With prompt_id == baseline.prompt_id and a baseline case failing its grader, NO false regression line is emitted (only the grader failure). With prompt differing but the baseline case still passing, no regression and exit 0. Rubber-stamp check: tampering a /tmp copy of pass.journey.json to break greeting's graders flips it to exit 1.

python3 scripts/selftest.py reported 220 passed, 0 failed (198 prior + 22 new llm expects). The block loads the runner via importlib, exercises grade() for every kind true and false plus unknown and no-graders, check_budgets() met and exceeded for cost/latency/pass-rate, find_regressions present/absent/prompt-unchanged, and drives run() over both fixtures (pass -> passed True pass_rate 1.0 no regressions; fail -> passed False with 'refund' in regressions). ./scripts/verify.sh printed GATE: GREEN (e8acad05e015341ff8458faa327216841a0eb67a).

Case-insensitive grep of the runner, both fixtures, wrapper, and README for bcengi/dejitech/travelpass/workpass/agentpass/coreconnect/onesim/mvne/dmitry/tripdesk/daybook/stripe/hubspot/ava returned zero matches. No em-dash (U+2014) or en-dash (U+2013) anywhere in the added diff. .warp/capabilities.yaml and plugin/templates/.warp/capabilities.yaml are byte-identical (sha256 4ec71fe88228e428fd1718e7b0df1a5adf6907bc40212284350654fb55ed86c7 both) and the llm_eval_runner entry is status: reference, not mechanical. The two 'dmitry' hits in the full commit diff are only the spec frontmatter owner field and the index table, outside AC5's runner/fixtures/wrapper/README scope.

This is the established house style across the file (20 such dividers, 19 predating this spec), is ASCII only (no em/en dash), lives in a code comment rather than shipped or outbound copy, is outside AC5's genericity scope (runner/fixtures/wrapper/README, all clean), and passes the repo's own docs-hygiene dash sweep which the gate ran GREEN. Non-defect; recorded for transparency.

summary: I confirmed HEAD == e8acad0, read the spec (AC1..AC5), manifest, runner, README, wrapper, both fixtures, the selftest llm block, and both capabilities files. I independently reran rather than trusting the manifest: drove the runner over pass.journey.json (exit 0) and fail.journey.json (exit 1, refund regression named), ran the wrapper (pass), ran scripts/selftest.py (220 passed / 0 failed), and ran scripts/verify.sh (GATE: GREEN bound to e8acad0). Adversarially I crafted /tmp journeys to probe every claim: no-graders (missing and empty) fail loud; each grader kind fails loud naming case+grader and passes when satisfied; unknown grader fails loud; cost/latency/pass-rate budgets each fail with the measured value; regression fires only when prompt_id differs from baseline (verified no false regression on unchanged prompt, correct regression naming both prompt_ids with other cases passing); tampering a fixture copy flips exit to 1; and fake_provider genuinely returns distinct per-case output (grading is not hardcoded). AC5 name/dash/capabilities sweeps are clean and the two capabilities files are byte-identical. I recomputed proof_digest twice = sha256:5195824a515867bb, matching the manifest. All five acceptance criteria are confirmed. The single note (an ASCII '# ---' comment divider following existing house style) is a non-defect, so the verdict is pass_with_notes.
